programmeRings.title: Programme follows the length of stay
programmeRings.alt: Three bands of rooms relate short, medium and overnight stays to a charging pause.
readings: Gym, clinic, reading room and workspace.
Rooms, showers and a shared kitchen.
programmeRings.note: The rings describe relationships and duration, not a fixed circular building.

nodePlace.title: The same connection, a stronger place
nodePlace.alt: The same charging connection shown before and after adding a public court and useful rooms.
readings: The same road, charging edge and vehicle access.
Rooms and open ground give people reasons to stay.
nodePlace.note: A spatial reading of the node–place relationship, not a plot of measured values.

fiveNeeds.title: Five needs made spatial
fiveNeeds.alt: Five small architectural spaces show comfort, relaxation, watching, participation and discovery.
readings: A seat away from vehicle movement.
A view of the life of the court.
Rooms to meet, eat, play and work.
Space that changes with markets and events.
fiveNeeds.note: Read left to right across the top row, then the lower row.

noPlug.title: Public life without a charging session
noPlug.alt: The same occupied public court with charging cars present and with every charging bay empty.
readings: Drivers join the life of the place.
The market, court and public rooms still have users.
noPlug.note: The test is whether a programme remains useful when every vehicle leaves.
details: Toilets and water; covered plaza; playground; community garden; emergency shelter; kiosk; grocery; parcel room; bike hub; laundromat; reading room; community hall; market; repair workshop; gym; workspace; clinic; childcare.
Waiting lounge; café; food hall; showers; drivers’ rooms.

groundSection.title: From dark lot to green ground
groundSection.alt: The same charging bay on exposed impermeable ground and beside a shaded walk with a rain garden.
readings: Heat, hard paving and nowhere to sit.
Canopy, seats, planting and water entering the soil.
groundSection.note: The spatial study is qualitative. The EPA temperature comparison remains in the preceding research figure.

accessLayers.title: Open ground, rooms with different access
accessLayers.alt: A U-shaped floor plan separates freely open court, rooms with opening hours, operated rooms and vehicle access.
readings: Court, shade, seats, water and a direct route from the street.
Reading room, hall, market and café.
Clinic, gym, childcare and drivers’ rooms.
accessLayers.note: The court stays reachable when individual rooms close; each operated room keeps its own hours.

catalogue.title: A catalogue of rooms
catalogue.alt: A kit of simple open-top rooms illustrates the programme catalogue without pictograms.
readings: 11 suit 20 minutes · 19 suit 1–2 hours · 6 suit a night.
11 suit a corridor · 20 suit a city · 17 suit a town.
catalogue.note: Counts from all 23 rows of Table 3.1. Stay and setting overlap. Nine examples shown, reading left to right: porch, washroom, market; reading room, hall, clinic; workspace, showers, sleeping room.

frameworkSteps.title: From site reading to a building
frameworkSteps.alt: Five site studies move from reading an existing site to choosing, arranging, operating and observing a Powerhouse.
readings: Count the network and the life around it.
Choose the corridor, city or town setting.
Place the court, rooms and charging edge.
Identify who uses each room and when.
Observe time, access and useful programme.
frameworkSteps.note: Read left to right across the top row, then the lower row. From Chapters 1–3 to a building tested in Graduate Thesis 01 and 02.

threeSettings.title: One type, three forms
threeSettings.alt: Simplified corridor, city and town programme axonometrics share an open public court and a single charging edge.
readings: Long truck bays; quieter rooms, showers and kitchen set back.
Compact and stacked; public rooms above an open street-level court.
Market, clinic and civic hall; a modest charging edge.
threeSettings.note: One programme logic, three arrangements. These studies are not at a common scale.

sixRules.title: Six spatial rules
sixRules.alt: Six architectural studies explain duration, the court-edge stall, separate routes, the open U, replaceable energy systems and green ground.
readings: Rooms fit the length of stay.
Vehicles arrive behind; people step into the court.
People and vehicle movement do not cross.
The public ground touches the street.
Replaceable systems support enduring public rooms.

dayClock.title: One plan across the day
dayClock.alt: Four matching floor plans show changing room occupancy in the morning, afternoon, evening and night.
readings: Residents, clinic visits, reading and play.
Food, shared rooms and evening events.
Waiting, washrooms and drivers on rest.
dayClock.note: Read left to right, top to bottom. An illustrative mixed-site day; Table 4.2 retains the separate corridor, city and town schedules, including a town night with no users.

threeMeasures.title: Three spatial observations
threeMeasures.alt: Three architectural observations show time spent beyond charging, freely accessible ground and programmes in use.
readings: Compare the person’s visit with the vehicle’s charging time.
Count space usable without buying or charging, safely reached on foot.
Check whether rooms meet a local need and work without charging.
threeMeasures.detailsTitle: Worked example — not measured site data
details: Vehicle charging: 35 min · person on site: 75 min · visitor without a vehicle: 50 min.
9 of 23 on site · 7 meet a local need · 7 work without charging.

powerCenter.title: From car-centred lot to public court
powerCenter.alt: Matched site plans contrast a car-centred commercial lot with an open public court and charging at one edge.
readings: Parking at the centre; stores reached from the car.
Public court at the centre; a direct pedestrian entrance and charging on the edge.
powerCenter.note: The same ground is reorganised around staying, with rooms wrapping an open U.

layerAssembly.title: Ground, charging, rooms, energy roof
layerAssembly.alt: Four separated architectural layers show permeable ground, charging edge, U-shaped public rooms and the energy roof.
readings: Stalls along one edge of the court.
A U with its street side open.
layerAssembly.note: A diagram of relationships; not a resolved construction assembly.
